title: Why Saharan Dust Secretly Feeds The Amazon
hook: A desert is secretly keeping the Amazon alive.
closing: A desert's dust feeds a rainforest, so protecting one far-off place quietly protects another.
question: Guessed dust could feed a rainforest?

segments.say: Winds lift 182 million tons of dust off the Sahara every year. That is a mountain of sand riding the sky.
About 27.7 million tons of it crosses the ocean and lands on the Amazon. The rest falls into the sea.
The Amazon loses 22,000 tons of phosphorus from its soil yearly. Saharan dust delivers the same, keeping the forest fed.
